name: Sci-fi tables
description: Random tables for science fiction: ship trouble, stations, salvage, aliens and contacts. Written for Fudger.

entities.name: Ship trouble
entities.description: What goes wrong aboard the ship.

entries.text: Life support smells of burnt coffee and nobody knows why
The navigation computer insists on a different route
A coolant leak in the engine room
The airlock cycles on its own at night
A stowaway is hiding in the cargo bay
Gravity flickers for [[1d6]] seconds every hour
The comms pick up a signal that sounds like the crew
A fuse box fails; half the lights go out

entities.name: Station rumours
entities.description: What people say in the bars of a space station.

entries.text: A mining company found something it is not reporting
The station's AI has started asking questions
A ship docked last week and nobody has seen its crew
Pirates are paying good money for navigation codes
Docking fees are going up again, and someone is pocketing the difference
A long-lost colony ship has been sighted near the gas giant
The medical bay is selling something that is not medicine
The security chief can be bought, but not cheaply

entities.name: Salvage
entities.description: What turns up in a wreck or a cargo crate.

entries.text: [[2d6]] crates of ration bars
A damaged but working scanner
A sealed data core
Spare parts worth a good price
A space suit with a name tag and a hole
A frozen pet in a stasis box
Encrypted credit chips
A crate of weapons with no serial numbers
A star map with one system circled
A crew log that stops in the middle of a sentence

entities.name: Alien features
entities.description: What stands out about an alien someone meets.

entries.text: Speaks only in questions
Changes colour with its mood
Has a smell that means something rude
Is very small and very loud
Moves only when nobody is watching
Carries its elders in a jar
Thinks humans are a kind of pet
Collects human songs
Sleeps standing up, in the middle of conversations
Is three beings that share one name
Finds handshakes deeply offensive
Pays for everything in stories

entities.name: Contacts
entities.description: Someone in a port who might help, for a price.

entries.text: A fixer who knows every dock worker.
A tired customs officer close to retiring
A ship mechanic who works for parts, not money
A smuggler with a fast ship and slow payments
A journalist chasing a story about a mining company
A bartender who hears everything:

entities.name: Deep space encounters
entities.description: What the sensors pick up between the stars.

entries.text: A distress beacon on an old frequency
A drifting freighter, lights on, no answer
[[1d3]] fighters closing fast without a transponder
A comet with a strange metal core
A patrol ship that wants to inspect the cargo
Nothing outside, but:
A field of debris:
Silence. Sensors show nothing at all, which should be impossible
